items.q: Is UCP the same as Google's Universal Cart?
items.a: No. UCP is the open Universal Commerce Protocol. Universal Cart is a Google shopping product, announced on 2026-05-19 and launched in the US on 2026-10-15, that uses UCP for checkout.

items.q: Does Google become the merchant of record?
items.a: No. In the spec and in Google's FAQ the business is the merchant of record and keeps financial liability and the order. Microsoft says the same for Copilot Checkout.

items.q: Is AP2 another name for UCP?
items.a: No. AP2 is an optional extension inside UCP, dev.ucp.common.payment.ap2_mandate since v2026-08-25. UCP says where the AP2 signatures go and AP2 defines the mandate formats. Live use of AP2 mandates in UCP is unverified as of 2026-10-20.
No. The platform gets an opaque token from a credential provider and passes it to the business, which charges it through its own PSP. Credentials flow one way.

items.q: Can an agent buy without the buyer pressing buy?
items.a: Not in the base protocol. Without the AP2 extension, the agent must hand the checkout to a trusted, deterministic UI where the buyer places the order.

items.q: Are UCP capabilities versioned independently since 2026-08-25?
items.a: Only third-party ones. The release notes speak of independent capability versioning, but the normative spec ties every dev.ucp capability to the release date; vendor extensions version on their own.

items.q: Is ES256 the only signature algorithm?
items.a: No. Every implementation must be able to verify ES256, and ES384 and EdDSA are optional.
Microsoft's page uses the future tense: Merchant Center will support UCP. Copilot Checkout already requires a UCP-compliant feed.

items.q: Where does a business publish its profile?
items.a: At /.well-known/ucp. The platform publishes its own profile at the URL it names in the UCP-Agent header.

items.q: What happens when a checkout needs something the API cannot collect?
items.a: The business returns requires_escalation with a continue_url and a message whose severity is requires_buyer_input or requires_buyer_review, and the platform opens continue_url for the buyer.

Google publishes no fee statement or schedule for UCP checkout on its surfaces. Shopify says its merchants pay only their standard payment processing fees in Google AI Mode and Gemini direct checkout, and Microsoft says it takes no commission on Copilot Checkout today. Google told The Register in January 2026 that it does not plan to take a cut (reported). Shopify's own terms reserve a possible Shopify fee for certain channels.
A Governing Council with permanent seats for Google and Shopify, an elected seat for Stripe and 2 open seats; Google holds the proxy vote for open seats until December 2028. There is no foundation.
Yes, two arXiv papers name it: 2606.05043 (Strabo) models UCP checkout, and 2602.06345 studies replay and context binding in UCP and AP2.

items.q: Does Google publish merchant numbers for UCP?
items.a: Only an order of magnitude. Google said on 2026-09-16 that UCP enables direct checkout for hundreds of thousands of brands and retailers across Google, without a definition; no exact count or transaction volume is published.
